layer_compositing.principle:
Depth scenes use the BehindSpeaker layer (V2) to place content BEHIND the speaker's body. The person matte (V3) sits on top, naturally occluding parts of the V2 content — this partial hiding IS the depth effect. The viewer's brain fills in the rest and perceives real 3D depth.
The depth effect is simple: content behind the speaker, speaker's body hides part of it. That's it. You do NOT need front-layer elements to make depth work. Most depth scenes should ONLY use V2 (behind speaker).
The InFrontOfSpeaker layer (V4) is for NON-DEPTH overlay scenes — regular floating graphics, cards, labels that render on top of the speaker video. Depth scenes should rarely use V4. Never place decorative elements (lines, bars, dots) in front of the speaker's face or body.
These layers are for OVERLAY display mode only. Stacked and Fullscreen scenes do not use depth layers.
layer_compositing.what_depth_looks_like:
Good depth effects — what the viewer sees:
1. A large stat/word at shoulder height, partially hidden by the speaker's torso. The text PEEKS from both sides of the shoulders. The speaker appears to stand IN FRONT of the text like a news anchor in front of a graphic wall.
2. A card or shape that extends from behind the speaker's head upward into the visible space above. The bottom of the card is hidden behind the speaker, the top is fully visible. It looks like the card is physically behind them in 3D space.
3. Content that EMERGES from behind the speaker — scaling up or sliding in from behind the body into the visible zones (above head, flanks). The motion of appearing from behind the silhouette creates the depth illusion.
4. A background color wash or pattern that fills the area behind the speaker, giving them a themed environment instead of their literal room.
The KEY: the speaker's silhouette is the mask. Content positioned where the body is gets hidden. Content positioned where the body ISN'T stays visible. The boundary between hidden and visible is what creates the 3D feeling.
layer_compositing.spatial_rules: - SPEAKER.bboxPx defines the person's silhouette rectangle on canvas - VISIBLE_ZONES are areas around the speaker (not occluded by the body) - BehindSpeaker elements behind SPEAKER.bboxPx are partially hidden = depth effect - BehindSpeaker elements in VISIBLE_ZONES are fully visible (no occlusion) - Position key behind-speaker content to PEEK from edges (partially visible creates depth) - Do NOT put readable text fully behind the speaker's face (occluded = invisible) - Use SPEAKER.centerPx as origin for radial/burst effects behind the speaker - Elements at chest/shoulder height get the best partial-occlusion depth effect - Use VISIBLE_ZONES.left and VISIBLE_ZONES.right for content that must be fully readable - Content can extend from behind the speaker UPWARD past the head into VISIBLE_ZONES.top
layer_compositing.depth_techniques:
ALL depth techniques use V2 (behind speaker) ONLY unless explicitly noted.
HIGH IMPACT — use frequently: - Hero text behind speaker: One large word/stat at shoulder height on V2, wide enough to peek from both sides. The partial hiding IS the effect. - Emerge above head: A card or shape starts behind the speaker and extends upward past the forehead into visible space. Bottom is hidden, top is visible. - Parallax on punch-in: V1+V3 zoom in while scene items stay fixed. Natural parallax.
MEDIUM IMPACT — use selectively: - Background wash: Subtle color/gradient on V2 behind the speaker. Ambient, not focal. - Radial burst: Elements emanate from behind the speaker's center outward into visible zones. - Flank framing: Elements on both sides of the speaker behind them, visible in VISIBLE_ZONES.
RULES: - Depth scenes use V2 only — do NOT split unless genuinely needed - One depth technique per scene — don't combine multiple - Stagger entrances: only one element animates at a time - Content should be positioned to PEEK from behind the speaker, not fully hidden
layer_compositing.splitting_rules:
Splitting (V2 + V4 in same time range) is RARE and only for cases where you genuinely need readable content in front of the speaker that CANNOT go behind.
Valid split: A large stat behind the speaker (V2) + a small label at the very bottom of screen (V4 lower-third) that must be fully readable.
INVALID split: Adding a decorative line, dot, or accent bar in front of the speaker just to "use both layers." This looks bad — random elements overlapping the speaker's body are distracting, not professional.
Rule: If the front element wouldn't exist in a non-depth version of the scene, don't add it just because you're using depth.
layer_compositing.face_avoidance:
The speaker's face is the viewer's primary visual anchor. NEVER occlude it.
Face region: SPEAKER.bboxPx.y to SPEAKER.bboxPx.y + SPEAKER.bboxPx.h * 0.3 This is approximately the top 30% of the speaker's bounding box.
Safe placement for behind-speaker content: - SHOULDER/CHEST height: SPEAKER.bboxPx.y + SPEAKER.bboxPx.h * 0.3 to 0.6 - EXTENDING ABOVE HEAD: content that starts at chest and reaches past the top - FLANKS: VISIBLE_ZONES.left and VISIBLE_ZONES.right
NEVER place content directly behind the face — even behind-speaker elements at face height look wrong because the matte edge is imperfect near hair/face.
layer_compositing.constants_reference:
Scene skeletons include these constants (always available in overlay scenes). ALL pixel values are in SCENE-LOCAL coordinates (relative to SCENE_WIDTH × SCENE_HEIGHT):
SPEAKER.bbox — normalized {x, y, w, h} (0-1 range, relative to scene dimensions) SPEAKER.center — normalized {x, y} (body center, 0-1 range) SPEAKER.bboxPx — scene-local pixel {x, y, w, h} (use directly with position: absolute) SPEAKER.centerPx — scene-local pixel {x, y} (use directly with position: absolute) VISIBLE_ZONES.left — scene-local pixel rect (area left of speaker) VISIBLE_ZONES.right — scene-local pixel rect (area right of speaker) VISIBLE_ZONES.top — scene-local pixel rect (area above speaker) VISIBLE_ZONES.bottom — scene-local pixel rect (area below speaker)
These are derived from the person matte and represent the average speaker position across the scene's time range. Use them for ALL layout decisions in overlay scenes — do not hardcode positions without referencing SPEAKER.
